answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days, whether the job is composing a sonnet or planning a voyage across the ocean. Bidding capacity scales with bonded funds, so splitting one deposit among fake identities adds no capacity. To field 1,000 identities with a $100 bond each, an attacker must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs even if every bond is returned.
